title: Acid Rain
objective: After this level you can explain what causes acid rain.
summary: Normal rain is about pH 5.6; acid rain, from sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides, is more than ten times as acidic. US power plant SO2 fell 96 percent, 1990 to 2023.

cards.headline: In 1852 a chemist found acid falling from factory-town skies.
cards.body: The Scottish chemist Robert Angus Smith studied rainwater near industrial cities in England and Scotland, and found acid rain. In 1872 his book Air and Rain laid it out. Where was the acid coming from?

cards.headline: All rain is a little sour
cards.body: Even clean rain isn't neutral. Carbon dioxide from the air dissolves in it and forms weak carbonic acid, giving normal rain a pH of about 5.6. Acid rain usually measures between 4.2 and 4.4. That gap looks small, but on Level 63's tenfold scale it's more than one full step: acid rain is more than ten times as acidic as normal rain.

cards.headline: Where the extra acid comes from
cards.body: The culprits are sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides. A little comes from volcanoes, but most comes from burning fossil fuels in power plants, vehicles and industry. In the air, these gases react with water, oxygen and other chemicals to form sulfuric and nitric acids. Then it all comes down as rain, snow, fog or even dry particles.

cards.headline: What it does on the ground
cards.body: Acid rain leaches aluminum out of soil and into lakes and streams, and strips away nutrients that trees need. At pH 5, most fish eggs can't hatch. It also eats at stone and metal, so statues and monuments slowly lose their carved detail.

cards.headline: A problem we largely cut
cards.body: The fix went after the source. The US Clean Air Act Amendments of 1990 created the Acid Rain Program, the first national cap-and-trade program: power plants got a cap on sulfur dioxide and could trade allowances. Between 1990 and 2023, annual sulfur dioxide emissions from US power plants fell by 96 percent (EPA).

cards.headline: Acid rain: traced
learned: Normal rain is about pH 5.6; acid rain usually 4.2 to 4.4
Sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides, mostly from fossil fuels, cause it
It harms lakes, forests and stone
US power plant sulfur dioxide fell 96 percent from 1990 to 2023

questions.prompt: Which two pollutants are the main causes of acid rain?

options.label: Carbon monoxide and methane
options.rationale: Neither forms the sulfuric and nitric acids in acid rain.

options.label: Ozone and helium
options.rationale: Helium is unreactive, and neither is the main cause.

options.label: Chlorine and ammonia
options.rationale: Neither is the main cause of acid rain.

questions.explanation: Sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides, mostly from burning fossil fuels, form sulfuric and nitric acids in the air.

questions.prompt: Clean, unpolluted rain has a pH of about 5.6. Why isn't it neutral?

options.label: Carbon dioxide dissolves in it and forms weak carbonic acid
Every raindrop picks up sulfur dioxide from factories
options.rationale: That is what turns normal rain into acid rain.

options.label: Lightning boils the rain on the way down
options.rationale: Boiling would not make rain acidic.

options.label: Raindrops dissolve salt from the sea
options.rationale: Salt does not make rain acidic.

questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide from the air dissolves in rain, forming weak carbonic acid, so normal rain is slightly acidic.

questions.prompt: Level 56's catalytic converter turns nitrogen oxides into nitrogen and oxygen. Why does that help the rain?

options.label: Nitrogen and oxygen neutralize acid already in clouds
options.rationale: The converter works on exhaust, not on clouds.

options.label: It stops carbon dioxide from reaching the air
options.rationale: The converter makes carbon dioxide; it doesn't remove it.

options.label: Nitrogen oxides form nitric acid, a cause of acid rain
It makes the rain fall less often
options.rationale: Acid rain is about what's in the rain, not how often it falls.

questions.explanation: In the air, nitrogen oxides form nitric acid, so converting them cuts one cause of acid rain.
